title: GKE Autopilot: what Google takes over and what it charges for

videos.script: Lesson 13 left you with nodes to choose, size and upgrade. Autopilot takes them away. This lesson is about what that costs, and what it forbids. {{takes}} With Autopilot, Google runs the nodes as well as the control plane. You describe pods. Google picks the machines. {{pays}} So the bill changes shape. You stop paying for nodes, full or empty. You pay for what each pod requests, while it runs. {{compare}} You will write a short program that prices the same pods both ways. Small, uneven services come out cheaper on Autopilot. Big, steady ones come out cheaper on Standard. {{refuses}} Then the price of not owning a node. No privileged containers, no host paths, no SSH. Most teams never miss them. A few workloads cannot run there at all. {{choose}} Last, four questions that decide between the two, before anything lands in production.
